name: Gouache app icon
summary: The app's own look, used only for the app icon: the same hand-painted gouache technique, simplified into big shapes that read at the size of a fingertip. It belongs to the app, not to any story; the app icon is made first from these words, and its two Android layers are edits of it.
medium: Opaque gouache on warm off-white watercolor paper, with a little colored-pencil texture for fur, grass and wood. Matte. No glossy highlights, no airbrushed gradients, no digital lens effects.
shapes: One chunky, rounded subject with a clear silhouette, big enough to fill most of the square, and almost no small details. Flat areas of color.
line: No black outlines. Edges come from color and value. Where a line helps, a thin colored-pencil line in a darker shade of the fill.
color: A limited palette per picture: 5 to 7 colors from the base palette plus the story's accents. Dusk and night are cool blues and lilacs, never black. Warm accents (the characters, the lights) pop against them.
light: One clear light idea per picture. Magical or warm lights (a glowing star, a porch lamp, fireflies) glow gold with a soft halo and light up the faces and things right next to them.
composition: One centered subject, everything that matters well inside the middle of the square, a calm background.
characters: No characters from any story: the icon is the app, not one book.
prompt: App icon painted in opaque, matte gouache on warm off-white paper, with a visible dry-brush texture and paper grain. One bold, chunky, rounded subject with a clear silhouette and almost no small details, so it reads at the size of a fingertip; flat areas of color, no outlines, edges made by color and value. One clear light idea: a warm gold glow with a soft halo against cool blues, never black.
avoid: Any text: letters, numbers, signs, labels, logos, watermarks, signatures, musical notes
Photorealism, 3D renders, glossy plastic or clay looks
Black outlines, comic halftones, anime styling
Pure black shadows, horror lighting, menacing silhouettes
Sharp teeth, claws on display, angry or scary faces
Extra or missing fingers, limbs, ears or tails; melted or merged shapes
Real brands, real people, existing characters
Copying the look of a named illustrator, an existing book or a studio
